items.subject: Petition for review of the order dated 21.6.2023 in Petition No. 10/TT/2019 to the extent of line length and commercial operation date of Asset -XXIV as declared by APTRANSCO. Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited

d. This Review Petition is liable to be dismissed for being barred by limitation
II. A party which chose not to appear during the proceedings cannot assail the
order in a review under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (the
“Code”)
a. The Review Petitioner has failed to appear or to file any pleadings in the proceedings
before this Commission pursuant to the Remand Order, culminating in the Impugned
Order.
b. The Review Petitioner consciously elected not to appear or file pleadings before this
Commission despite multiple opportunities. The finality of litigation is a cardinal
principle of law which the Petitioner seeks to militate against. Consequently, now to
seek to assail the Impugned Order by way of review is a clear abuse of the process
of law. In these circumstances, the Petition is disentitled to institute proceedings for
review of the Impugned Order.
III. No grounds for review are made out in the case, as there is -
a. There is no error apparent on the face of the record. The Review Petitioner has not
pointed out any material or documents or fact from the record of this Commission
that has not been considered in the Impugned Order. The averments in the Petition
and the documents filed in support were never a part of the record of this

Commission. Accordingly, there is no error apparent on the face of the record in this
case.
• No new or additional material was placed on record which was not within the
knowledge of the Petitioner.
a. Order 47, Rule 1 requires that additional or new evidence can be taken into
consideration in review only when such evidence was not within the knowledge of
the Petitioner or could not be discovered by ordinary due diligence in the original
proceedings. The Petitioner has only relied on the order dated 7 November 2021
passed by this Commission in Petition No. 265/TT/2019. The Petitioner was a party
before this Commission in those proceedings and was well aware of its existence
prior to the passing of the Impugned Order.
IV. The length and commercial operation date of Asset XXIV are undisputed and
admitted
a. The Impugned Order records the length and commercial operation date of Asset
XXIV as 71.32Km and 17 October 2012, respectively. These facts were duly pleaded
in the Original Petition and in the Appeal before APTEL. Similarly, the commercial
operation date of Asset XXIV was duly set out in the Appeal.
b. Order dated 27 April 2022 in the DFR No. 378 of 2021 & IA No. 1682 of 2021 records
that the Review Petitioner did not wish to dispute any factual averments in the Appeal
since it relinquished the right to file a reply to the Appeal. Consequently, the Review
Petitioner expressly admits the averments in the Appeal, including the facts set out
above. The Review Petitioner, therefore, cannot contend to the contrary in any
proceeding.

Rejoinder to the Reply of APTRANSCO, submitted by the Review Petitioner
11. In response to the reply filed by Respondent No. 1, the Review Petitioner, in its
rejoinder dated 10.12.2024, has filed issue-wise submissions as under:
(a) As regards limitations, the Review Petitioner has submitted that there has been
a delay of mere 87 days in filing the said Review Petition, as the date of filing as
mentioned on the CERC’s portal is 30.10.2023. The duration from 30.10.2023 to
18.06.2024 is attributable to administrative delay caused by extension of the scrutiny
period of the Petition, which is not the Petitioner’s fault. As a government company,
the Petitioner has various levels of departmental scrutiny to undertake, which cannot
be overlooked before the concerned person signs any document. After multiple rounds
of discussion within various departments and coordination with the legal counsels
present in Delhi, the decision was taken to file a Review Petition, which inadvertently
consumed a lot of time and caused an unintentional delay. In support, reliance has
been placed on the Hon’ble Supreme Court order in G. Ramegowda v. Spl. Land
Acquisition Officer [(1988) 2 SCC 142]. The provisions regarding filing of a Review
Petition as mentioned in Rule 1 of Order 47 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 do not
preclude any party who did not appear during the proceedings that led to the
Impugned Order from challenging such an order in review. No party is excluded from
filing an application for review of an Order, let alone a party who was inadvertently
absent from the proceedings leading to the said Order.
(b) As regards the grounds for review, the Review Petitioner has highlighted that
the Impugned Order dated 21.06.2023 in Petition No. 10/TT/2019 has erroneously
mentioned the line length and the commercial operation date of Asset XXIV to be
